purpose: Review records for the existing beginner-facing classification and responsibility block.

primaryText.hebrew: ארבעה אבות נזיקין השור הבור המבעה וההבער
primaryText.editorialNormalization: Opening list excerpted for guided category reading.

translation.text: There are four primary categories of damage: ox, pit, maveh, and fire.

encounters.learnerLevel: Beginner learning to read a legal classification as an argument rather than as isolated vocabulary.
encounters.learningObjective: Name the categories before inferring that they function alike.

languageSupport.grammarNote: A list may establish categories whose differences will matter in the next move.
languageSupport.translationPath: Guided English remains visible alongside the source.

encounters.context: The opening Mishnah introduces a classification of damages. Seder uses it to teach source structure, not to determine responsibility in a real incident.

assessment.bestAnswer: First name the categories, then look for the feature that makes each distinct.
assessment.rationale: The source begins by sorting; a learner should not erase distinctions before reading them.
misconceptions: Assuming the first category controls every later case.
Treating the list as a story rather than a classification.
assessment.transferPrompt: For an unfamiliar classification, record the named categories before asking what they share or how they differ.

encounters.safetyBoundary: Text study only; this does not determine liability, payment, or halakhic responsibility for any real case.

review.secondSourceContext: The same opening passage contrasts categories and later identifies a common denominator, giving a second context for the reading move.
review.retrievalTrigger: Weekly review or a missed category-map item.

primaryText.hebrew: לא הרי השור כהרי המבעה ... הצד השוה שבהן שדרכן להזיק ושמירתן עליך
primaryText.editorialNormalization: Two short excerpts combined only for a guided comparison exercise.

translation.text: Ox is not like maveh ... their common denominator is that they cause damage and their safeguarding is upon you.

encounters.learnerLevel: Beginner ready to compare categories without making them identical.
encounters.learningObjective: Distinguish a relevant difference from a stated common principle.

languageSupport.grammarNote: First identify the contrast; then ask what the source explicitly says is shared.
languageSupport.translationPath: Guided English remains visible; a literal gloss may be opened on request.

encounters.context: The Gemara's classification work preserves differences while drawing a limited common principle. This is a textual-reasoning exercise, not a procedure for actual claims.

assessment.bestAnswer: A shared principle can connect categories without erasing the feature that made the contrast necessary.
assessment.rationale: The sequence models classification through both distinction and connection.
misconceptions: Treating a common denominator as proof that all cases have identical details.
Treating every difference as a rejection of all connection.
assessment.transferPrompt: In a fresh source, state one named difference and one stated common principle before offering an explanation.

encounters.safetyBoundary: The lesson explains the source's reasoning; it gives no legal or financial advice for a real dispute or accident.

review.secondSourceContext: The learner later meets the same move in a fresh classification exercise, rather than a reordered copy of this question.
review.retrievalTrigger: Return after a missed distinction-versus-common-ground prompt.
